reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the first three premises by demonstrating that low-temperature, diffusion-limited conditions lead to stochastic, single-phase HEA formation and that multimetallic mixtures favor this over bimetallic ones. However, the premises linking single-phase structure to uniform active site distribution and superior catalytic performance are not addressed in the cited passages; they are asserted without specific prior evidence.
premises: Low-temperature reduction inhibits precursor mobility, forcing stochastic incorporation of elements.
Stochastic incorporation promotes single-phase HEA nanoparticle formation.
Combining multiple elements favors single-phase formation compared to bimetallic systems.
Single-phase HEA nanoparticles have a more uniform distribution of active sites.
Uniform active site distribution leads to superior catalytic performance over bimetallic systems.
